kurz: Why knowledge of the economy rarely pays off as a forecast, and why valuation, the level of interest rates, risk-bearing capacity and three checking questions before every decision are more reliable.

bloecke.md:
Macro data are public. The ifo index is published for everyone at the same minute, and so is the inflation figure. Every price you see afterwards already contains the conclusions that all market participants have drawn from them. To make money with economic data, you therefore need two correct assessments. The first concerns the economy, the second the part of it that is not yet reflected in the price.

The second assessment is the more difficult one. Destatis (the Federal Statistical Office) reported an inflation rate of 2.9% for August 2026, and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported 3.4% on 11 September, unchanged from July. Little happened on the markets as a result. The figures were not unimportant, but they were in line with expectations. Prices react to the deviation from the [[consensus expectation]], not to the value itself.
A macro opinion only becomes an investment idea when it deviates from the priced-in expectation and when you can state by how much and by when.

## Limits of point forecasts

First, it is precisely the turning points that forecasts usually miss. Between June 2024 and June 2025, the ECB cut its deposit facility rate in eight steps from 4.00% to 2.00%. Investors who derived from this the obvious rule that the interest rate cycle was pointing downwards were wrong twelve months later. In June 2026, the ECB raised the rate to 2.25%. On 10 September 2026, it decided to raise it to 2.50%, effective from 16 September. The Fed followed on 16 September with its first rate rise since 2023, to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, effective from the following day. The rate rises were triggered by an energy price shock that no economic model had indicated. The price of Brent rose from $109.51 on 9 September to $130.80 on 15 September, that is, by just over 19% in four trading days.

Second, the sample is very small. The best-known rule of economic analysis states that an inverted yield curve heralds a recession. In the US, it rests on around a dozen cases since 1955, with lead times of between six and twenty-four months and two false alarms, in 1966 and after the long inversion from 2022 to 2024. Twelve observations are enough for a hypothesis, but not for a trading signal. The Sahm rule was triggered in 2024 without a recession following. Its inventor had explicitly intended it as a real-time description of the situation, not as a forecasting model.

Third, there are too many intermediate steps between forecast and investment result. Even if the economy is assessed correctly, it remains open which price reacts and how. The year 2025 shows this. Over the course of the year, the ECB cut the deposit facility rate by a full percentage point, from 3.00% to 2.00%. The yield on German bonds outstanding (Umlaufrendite) rose in the same year from 2.31% to 2.78%. The central bank sets the short-term rate, the market determines the long-term rate.

bloecke.titel: Key interest rate and long-term interest rate compared
bloecke.unter: ECB deposit facility rate (level at year-end) and yield on German bonds outstanding (year-end close), for 2026 in each case as of mid-September.

bloecke.md:
For the price effect, the rule of thumb is: price change ≈ − duration × change in interest rates.

A bond position with a duration of seven years loses around 3.3% of its market value when yields rise by 0.47 percentage points (7 × 0.47). This happened in 2025, even though the ECB cut interest rates that year. Investors who had correctly foreseen the rate cuts and then bought long maturities had answered the macro question correctly and the portfolio question wrongly. (Illustrative calculation; real funds differ depending on duration and composition.)

## Three variables you can read off

Three variables are superior to a forecast because you do not have to estimate them. They can be read off.

The first is the **valuation level**. The Shiller P/E (CAPE) of the S&P 500 stood at 40.94 on 18 September 2026. The historical mean is 17.42, the median 16.13. This is not a sell signal. The value says something about the expected return over the next ten years, but practically nothing about the next twelve months. From 2017 to 2026, the CAPE was almost continuously above 27, and investors who got out because of this missed one of the strongest bull markets in history. The right consequence of a high valuation level is a more cautious return assumption in your own plan, not a sale.

bloecke.titel: Shiller P/E of the S&P 500, as of 18 Sep 2026
bloecke.unter: A level close to the dotcom record of 44.19 lowers the expected long-term return, but says nothing about the next twelve months.

bloecke.md: The second variable is the **level of interest rates**. The interest rate is the yardstick against which every other investment has to be measured, and today it is at a completely different level from five years ago. The ten-year Bund yielded 3.52% on 18 September 2026, after reaching 3.58% on 15 and 16 September, its highest level since 2011. At the end of 2021, the yield on German bonds outstanding was minus 0.28%. What matters, however, is the [[real interest rate]], measured against expected inflation rather than past inflation. In September 2026, the ECB projected inflation for the euro area of 3.0% (2026), 2.5% (2027) and 2.1% (2028). After deducting these expectations, around one to one and a half percentage points of the 3.52% remain in real terms, depending on the horizon. At the short end, the calculation is less favourable. A deposit facility rate of 2.50% with German inflation at 2.9% gives a slightly negative real interest rate. Instant-access savings accounts pay interest again in 2026, but do not yet deliver any gain in purchasing power.

bloecke.formel: Real interest rate ≈ nominal interest rate − expected inflation
bloecke.erklaerung: Fisher approximation. The exact relationship is (1 + i) = (1 + r) × (1 + π), with i as the nominal interest rate, r as the real interest rate and π as expected inflation. The previous year's inflation is the wrong variable, because the decision concerns the future.
variablen: nominal interest rate of the investment
expected inflation over the same term
bloecke.beispiel: A Bund yield of 3.52% with expected inflation of 2.1% gives around 1.4 percentage points in real terms. At the end of 2021, a nominal minus 0.28% was set against inflation of 3.1%, giving around minus 3.4 percentage points in real terms.

bloecke.md: The third variable is your own [[risk-bearing capacity]]. It is the only one of the three variables that you know yourself and nobody else does. What needs to be clarified is how secure your income is and how strongly it depends on the same business cycle as your portfolio. An engineer in the supplier industry and a teacher with civil servant status bear completely different risks with an identical portfolio. According to revised figures, German industrial production in July 2026 was 1.8% below its level a year earlier, and in August the number of unemployed exceeded three million for the second month in a row. Employees in cyclical sectors already bear economic risk through their salary and should not double it in their portfolio. This assessment is possible without knowing the future course of the economy.

## Taxes on getting out

In Germany, sales made for macroeconomic reasons are more than a rebooking, because they trigger taxes. When you sell an equity fund portfolio, for example to avoid a recession, a capital gain arises that is taxable as investment income (Section 16(1) no. 3 and Section 19 InvStG, Investment Tax Act; Section 20(1) no. 3 EStG, Income Tax Act). This is subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) under Section 32d(1) EStG plus a solidarity surcharge of 5.5% on that tax, 26.375% in total, or more if you are liable for church tax. The 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) for equity funds (Section 20(1) InvStG) and the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 (Section 20(9) EStG) reduce the tax, but do not eliminate it.

bloecke.titel: Net proceeds after selling an equity fund portfolio
bloecke.unter: Calculated for a portfolio value of €100,000, acquisition costs of €60,000, an equity fund with 30% partial exemption, a fully available saver's allowance and no church tax.

bloecke.formel: Required price decline = 1 − net proceeds / portfolio value
bloecke.erklaerung: The market has to fall by this percentage for the net proceeds to buy the same number of fund units again. Only a larger decline produces a gain.
bloecke.beispiel: 1 − 92,878.75 / 100,000 = 7.12%. A decline of 5% is therefore not enough. Buying back at minus 5% means a loss despite a correct forecast.

bloecke.md: When you buy back, the holding period starts with a new, higher purchase price. Part of the tax paid would therefore have become due later anyway. Getting out brings the payment forward, so the tax is not entirely lost. What is lost is the return on the €7,121 in the meantime and the option of never having to make the sale at all. With 30 years remaining, this loss of compound interest is the larger item.

## Thinking in scenarios

The ECB does not publish a point forecast in the sense in which investors would use one either. Its projections are based on technical assumptions about oil prices and exchange rates. If an assumption changes, the projection changes too, and an oil price jump of 19% within six days does not feature in any baseline scenario. It therefore makes sense to reverse the question. Instead of considering what will happen, you check which states the portfolio has to survive.

Three scenarios are usually enough: persistent inflation with rising interest rates, inflation returning to target with moderate growth, and a slump in demand with falling interest rates and falling profits. For each scenario, you write down what happens to your portfolio and your income. An allocation that remains bearable in all three cases is superior to one that is optimal in the most likely case and forces you to give up in the least likely one.

schritte.titel: Clarify the thesis and the market expectation
schritte.text: The thesis needs a number and a date. “Interest rates will keep rising” is not enough as a thesis. In mid-September 2026, the money markets were already pricing in an ECB deposit facility rate of just under 2.9% for December 2026. A position on rising interest rates only makes a profit above this mark. Investors who do not know this mark can lose even when interest rates rise.

schritte.titel: Define the change and its costs
schritte.text: Position size, tax, spread and reinvestment need to be clarified. If the honest answer is “I'll sell everything”, the issue is your own risk-bearing capacity and not a macro decision. Risk-bearing capacity should be decided independently of the current market situation.

Decide in advance which value, by what date, would refute the thesis and what then happens. Without a re-entry rule, a tactical position turns into a permanent exit, the most expensive mistake when using macro knowledge.

bloecke.md: The most common mistake is getting out without a defined point for getting back in. Historically, six to twenty-four months passed between the inversion of the yield curve and the start of a recession, during which shares often continued to rise. Investors who sell at the signal and wait for the all-clear are waiting for information that only exists in hindsight. The NBER often dates US recessions only with a delay of a year.

In professional investing, there are cases in which macro positions work. They differ systematically from the way private investors proceed:

- The time horizon is short and the question narrow, for example a single interest rate decision that is traded through money market futures and not through the entire portfolio.
- The position is small, separate from long-term wealth and has a maximum loss defined in advance.
- The advantage lies in interpreting the data, because everyone knows the data themselves. Money is made from a more precise breakdown, for example into headline and core inflation. In August 2026, the US headline rate was 3.4% and the core rate 2.4%. Measured by the consumer price index (CPI), this is therefore a pure supply shock without broad domestic price pressure. The situation is thus clearly different from 2022, even if the headlines look similar.
- The exit rule is fixed before the position is entered.

For a portfolio that is meant to fund retirement provision, hardly any private macro idea meets these four conditions. Macro knowledge nevertheless remains useful, for putting the situation into context rather than as a reason to reallocate.

mitnehmen: Macro knowledge helps you understand the economy, but does not give you an edge in the market, because prices already contain the consensus expectation and only the deviation from it is traded.
Even a correct economic forecast is not enough; in 2025 the ECB cut the deposit facility rate by a full percentage point, while the yield on German bonds outstanding rose by 0.47 points.

The valuation level, the level of interest rates and your own risk-bearing capacity can be read off and do not have to be forecast; they belong in the assumptions of your plan, not in buy and sell signals.

Getting out of an equity fund portfolio with a book gain of €40,000 costs around €7,121 in tax after the partial exemption and saver's allowance, so the market has to fall by more than 7% before the switch ends without a loss.
Before every macro decision, it should be clear what is priced in, what the switch costs and how you will recognise that you were wrong.

begriffe.text: The value that analysts and market participants expect on average for a figure not yet published. Prices already reflect it; price movements only arise from a deviation from it.

Nominal interest rate minus expected inflation over the same term (Fisher approximation). Only the real interest rate measures the gain in purchasing power. A deposit facility rate of 2.50% is negative in real terms with inflation at 2.9%.

Method in which, instead of a point forecast, several possible states are described and the consequences for the portfolio and income are examined for each. The aim is an allocation that remains bearable in all cases.

The degree of fluctuation and loss that someone can withstand without having to abandon the plan. It depends on the investment horizon, the liquidity buffer and how dependent your own income is on the business cycle.

Flat-rate compensation under Section 20 InvStG for the tax already paid at fund level. For privately held investments, 30% of the income from equity funds is exempt, 15% for mixed funds and 0% for bond and money market funds.
